outcomes.O1: CANDIDATE THREAD: a PM scans today's Trending x Price list by company name and classification, opens one name, and reads its header as four cards and its Thesis as three cards, each opening a modal -- one journey on one screen family.
outcomes.O2: A PM identifies every ranked security by company name, asset class, sub-asset class and sector, and sees how far it moved in rank since the last run, in the Positioning Holdings Breakdown pattern.
outcomes.O3: A PM reads how names moved over time in a chart that stays legible at ten or more names, labelled by name.
outcomes.O4: A PM reads a selected security's headline figures as four stable cards (Price, Financials, Market features, Trading technicals), each opening a modal, every figure in the security's own currency.
outcomes.O5: A PM reads a security's timeline spine: dated publications, events and headlines with a keyword cloud, led by Opal Data Harvest and supplemented by the News Scanner.
outcomes.O6: A PM reads the Thesis as Investment thesis / Risks / Recommendation cards beneath the principal chart, each opening a modal with its evidence, and can tell where each citation came from and whose recommendation it is.
outcomes.O7: A PM sees who runs the company on Exec Management for every covered name, with the source named, even when the filing's officer section is empty.
outcomes.O8: A PM reads Peers as a clean comparable table with readable tickers and the absent columns disclosed once, without internal strings.
outcomes.O9: A PM reads the Model sheet with plain line names, and each refused line says in one sentence whether the data or the display is missing.
outcomes.O10: A PM reads Posture as a verdict card with reason cards, or a designed empty state when there is no call -- never a paragraph of machine reasoning.
outcomes.O11: A reviewer cannot tell the page from /market or /positioning: shared footer (timestamp | Source), shared dialog, shared panel states and shared chart palette, legend and tooltip, with no raw codes on the face.
